title_en: Meredith Whitney, Founder and CEO, Meredith Whitney Advisors
title_zh: Meredith Whitney：Meredith Whitney Advisors 创始人兼 CEO
subtitle_zh: 从次级贷款到 K 型经济，Whitney 拆解美国消费者信贷收紧与 AI 资本开支风险
description: Meredith Whitney, Founder and CEO, Meredith Whitney Advisors

turns.en: So what's happened is, I would say 50% of households have to go to other means, they've had to go to other means to get loans. Now, I'm not saying they're not banked, banks will take deposits. They'll give you a debit card, but they're less and less going to give you a credit card.
turns.zh: 所以现在的实际情况是，我会说有一半的家庭不得不另想办法、不得不通过其他渠道去借钱。我不是说他们没有银行账户，银行还是会收存款、会给你一张借记卡（debit card），但越来越少愿意给你信用卡（credit card）了。

turns.en: They're definitely not going to give you a home equity loan, and very rarely will they give you other type of lending products.
turns.zh: 他们绝对不会给你房屋净值贷款（home equity loan），其他类型的信贷产品也很少会给。

turns.en: Hello, this is Dean Kurnut and welcome to the Alpha Exchange, where we explore topics in financial markets associated with managing risk, generating return, and the deployment of capital, and the alternative investment industry.
turns.zh: 大家好，我是 Dean Curnutt，欢迎收听 Alpha Exchange。在这档节目里，我们探讨金融市场中与管理风险、创造回报、资本配置以及另类投资（alternative investment）行业相关的话题。

turns.en: My guest today on the Alpha Exchange is Meredith Whitney. She is the founder and CEO of Meredith Whitney Advisers, and someone who needs almost no introduction. Meredith, it's great to welcome you to the podcast today. Well, thanks for having me. Yeah, I'm really looking forward to this. We were introduced by our mutual friend,
turns.zh: 今天我请到的嘉宾是 Meredith Whitney。她是 Meredith Whitney Advisors 的创始人兼 CEO，几乎不需要多做介绍。Meredith，非常欢迎你今天来到我们的播客。——谢谢你邀请我。是啊，我很期待这次对谈。我们是经由一位共同的朋友介绍的，

turns.en: Louis Gav. I'm very glad he made that introduction, and I'm glad you took up the invite. Louis could ask me for just about anything, and I did for him. He's just a force. There's no one like Louis and his group, and his father is the Mick Jagger of Finance. And just tremendous thought process on macro, very differentiated,
turns.zh: Louis Gave。我很高兴他牵了这个线，也很高兴你接受了邀请。Louis 让我帮什么忙都行，我也确实帮了。他就是这么有号召力。没有人能像 Louis 和他的团队那样，他父亲可以说是金融界的 Mick Jagger。他对宏观（macro）的思考非常了不起、非常与众不同，

turns.en: I've always enjoyed the conversations with him as well. So let's just start with you and your background. You're famous for a couple of things, but one of which is I want to say it's the last day of October in 2007, asking out loud, will city need to cut its dividend?
turns.zh: 我一直也很享受跟他的交流。那我们就从你和你的背景聊起吧。你因为几件事而闻名，其中一件是——我记得那是 2007 年 10 月的最后一天——你公开发问：Citi 会不会需要削减股息（dividend）？

turns.en: And I just look back. I think the stock was down 6% on the year, and it fell another 99% to its lows. But what was really interesting was that the S&P was at an all-time high. Financials weren't, but the S&P was at an all-time high in October of 2007.
turns.zh: 回头来看，我记得当时那只股票年内跌了 6%，之后又一路跌到低点，再跌了 99%。但真正有意思的是，标普 500（S&P 500）当时正处于历史高点。金融股不是，但 2007 年 10 月标普 500 确实在历史最高位。

turns.en: You saw what was happening in city, and then just the implications for the broader economy. Take us back even to the 90s. You grew up analyzing finance, specialty finance in the 90s at Oppenheimer. Take us just back to the early parts of your career, because what I want to do in this
turns.zh: 你看到了 Citi 内部正在发生的事，以及它对更广泛经济的影响。带我们回到 90 年代吧。你是在 90 年代于 Oppenheimer 分析金融、尤其是特殊金融（specialty finance）成长起来的。带我们回到你职业生涯的早期，因为在这次

turns.en: conversation is lean on some of that, what you developed as a capacity to look around corners. Let's start out first with the fact that I was a history major from a liberal arts college, getting into finance. And I always assumed that everybody was smarter than me, that everybody
turns.zh: 对话里我想借重的，正是你培养出的那种「看清拐角后面」的能力。——先说说我其实是从一所文理学院的历史专业毕业、然后进入金融行业的。我一直以为每个人都比我聪明，以为每个人

turns.en: had an engineering and math degree. I was smart enough to know early on that it didn't matter if I looked smart. I got too weak, maybe just kind of like a month, where I cared. I really was so nervous, and I cared what I looked like. I was afraid to look dumb. And I quickly got over
turns.zh: 都拿着工程和数学学位。我很早就聪明地意识到，看起来聪明并不重要。我有过——也许就那么一个月——很在意的阶段。我当时真的特别紧张，很在意自己的形象，怕显得蠢。但我很快就

turns.en: that, because if you're not afraid to ask questions and appear dumb, you're never going to learn. And being smart is a moving target. I always think that I have such an uphill battle to climb in terms of getting information and learning in general. And I took that approach very early on.
turns.zh: 克服了这一点，因为如果你不怕提问、不怕显得蠢，你就永远学不到东西。而且「聪明」是个不断移动的目标。我总觉得在获取信息、在学习这件事上，我要爬的坡很陡。我很早就采取了这种态度。

turns.en: So being a history major, it's how I put things together. So I want to understand what came before an event, why things happened, what are the pieces that could allow things to happen again, or what are the pieces that could allow things not to happen again? What is so
turns.zh: 所以作为历史专业出身，这就是我串联信息的方式。我想搞清楚一件事之前发生了什么、事情为什么会发生、哪些因素会让它重演，或者哪些因素能让它不再重演。真正

turns.en: fantastic. So I worked in oil and gas for the first, I'd say, year. And the first thing I did was read in Newergens the prize. Fortunately, the oil and gas industry wasn't that old at the time. It was 150 years at that time. And then I went into financial services because the
turns.zh: 了不起的地方在于……所以我第一年在油气（oil and gas）行业做研究。我做的第一件事就是读 Daniel Yergin 的《The Prize》。幸运的是，当时油气行业历史还不算太长，也就 150 年。后来我转到了金融服务行业，因为

All of my friends are just working in investment banking and we're working their tails off. That's what I thought you did. And in fact, that's what you can be smarter than me, but I work
turns.zh: 我跟着做的那位油气分析师觉得我太激进，是想抢他的饭碗。我当时才 23 岁。我所有的朋友都在投资银行（investment banking）工作，累死累活。我以为这行就该这么干。事实上就是——你可以比我聪明，但我

turns.en: you every time. So says Mayor Michael Bloomberg. And anyway, then I'm fallen to financial services. And what's important about that, especially if there was bank analysts in the early 90s, and then there were especially finance analysts. And what that included was the brokerage firms,
turns.zh: 每次都比你更拼。这话是 Michael Bloomberg 市长说的。总之，后来我转到了金融服务。这一点很重要，尤其在 90 年代初有银行分析师，然后还有特殊金融分析师。这个领域涵盖的包括券商（brokerage firms），

And so what I loved about finance is it's so data driven because it's so data driven, you can be really granular and really right. Now the timing's always
turns.zh: 资产管理公司、单一险种保险公司（monolines）、信用卡公司、次级贷款（subprime），也就是次级车贷、次级房屋净值贷款、各种次级产品。我喜欢金融的地方就在于它非常数据驱动（data driven），正因为数据驱动，你可以做得非常精细、非常准确。当然时机永远

turns.en: the big if, but it takes more than just that, but it was fascinating. I never wanted to leave my seat to go get my MBA or anything because I felt so grateful and fortunate to have that seat at the table with what I thought were some of the smartest people and also some of the most suspect people.
turns.zh: 是最大的变数，而且光靠准还不够，但这真的很迷人。我从没想过离开我的位置去读 MBA 什么的，因为我觉得能坐在这个桌子上、跟我认为最聪明同时也最可疑的一群人共事，实在是既感激又幸运。

turns.en: That's the background of how I started. And it was really just to get to the truth. This was before Dodd-Frank where you could have analysts, analysts decided whether you were going to do an investment banking deal or not. It was my job to give my boss reasons not to do deals because it takes a
turns.zh: 这就是我入行的背景。说到底就是为了追求真相。那还是在《多德-弗兰克法案》（Dodd-Frank）之前，那时候分析师可以——由分析师来决定你要不要做一单投行业务。我的职责就是给老板列出「不该做这些交易」的理由，因为建立声誉要花

turns.en: lifetime to build a reputation in a moment to destroy it. And so the right and wrong aspect I grew up with and it was allowed for under the team I worked for, which was fantastic. A lot of famously analysts did deals that were stinkers and that was just not something that was tolerated
turns.zh: 一辈子，毁掉它却只要一瞬间。所以这种是非观是我一路成长中养成的，而且在我所在的团队里是被允许、被鼓励的，这非常棒。很多出名的分析师做了一些烂交易（stinkers），而那种行为在我们这里是不会被容忍的，

turns.en: that would fly. So it was very fortunate that I love what I did and then from a values perspective there was such a strategic fit. There seems like there was an especially large amount of independence coming from that particular group at Oppenheimer at the time. There was just this investigation
turns.zh: 根本行不通。所以我很幸运，我热爱自己做的事，从价值观角度看契合度也非常高。——当时 Oppenheimer 那个团队似乎表现出特别强的独立性。对一批特殊金融公司正在进行一场调查，

turns.en: into a lot of these specialty finance companies. I was just going back. I was remembering. I think it was called green tree. I'm remembering the money store. I'm a big Yankees fan and grew up listening to Phil Rosuto and I was going back. He did a commercial in 1984. It was all about
turns.zh: 针对很多这类特殊金融公司。我刚在回想，我记得有一家叫 Green Tree，还有 Money Store。我是 Yankees 的铁杆球迷，从小听着 Phil Rizzuto 的解说长大，我又回想起——他在 1984 年拍过一个广告，讲的全是

turns.en: second mortgage loan capital where you could borrow against your home and he was presenting a great deal at 14.5%, which is just mind boggling how high rates were back then. And you tell me if this is correct, but in studying things like subprime autos and just the Byzantine of the capital structures
turns.zh: 二次抵押贷款（second mortgage），你可以拿房子抵押借钱，他在广告里推销一笔「超划算」的贷款，利率 14.5%——当时的利率高得令人咋舌。你帮我看看对不对：正是通过研究次级车贷这类东西、研究那些错综复杂（Byzantine）的资本结构，

turns.en: and just the way in which the accounting goes, it seems like that sets you up very well for that period leading into the GFC that allowed you to just take a differentiated view to see things that clearly others weren't seeing at the time. In the same way, some things applied and some
turns.zh: 以及那些会计处理的门道，这似乎为你很好地铺垫了通往全球金融危机（GFC）的那段时间，让你能提出与众不同的观点，看到别人当时明显没看到的东西。同样的道理，有些经验适用，有些

turns.en: things were different. And I got my MBA on the job by covering subprime and on subprime because what happened in the 90s right when I started was that securitization moved beyond the mortgage back security into other asset classes like auto loans, like credit card loans, any type of commercial
turns.zh: 则不一样。我其实是靠覆盖次级贷款、在次级贷款这块「在职读了个 MBA」，因为我刚入行的 90 年代发生的事是：证券化（securitization）从住房抵押贷款支持证券（MBS）扩展到了其他资产类别，比如车贷、信用卡贷款、各种商业

turns.en: lease. It expanded the pie. And because of that, because it was cheap financing comparable to banks, the pie of consumers that were catered to you also expanded. One of the things that you get with securitization data that you didn't get from banks at the time and others that didn't
turns.zh: 租赁。它把蛋糕做大了。正因为如此，因为相比银行这是更便宜的融资，被服务到的消费者群体这块蛋糕也扩大了。证券化数据能给你一样当时银行、以及其他不做

turns.en: securitize was monthly data. And you have monthly pools that you can look at a 30-day delinquencies and track where you think losses are going. And also losses. And then the size of the pools and could be so granular about who the winners were and who the losers were in ways that you could
turns.zh: 证券化的机构给不了你的东西，那就是月度数据。你有按月划分的资产池（pool），可以看 30 天逾期率（30-day delinquencies），追踪你认为损失会走向何方，还有实际损失、资产池的规模，可以非常精细地看出谁是赢家、谁是输家，精细到你几乎

turns.en: almost see. The data's gotten out so perfect that the credit spreads move and tandem. But at the time, this was a brand new world. The harder you worked, the more you dove into the data, the critical advantage you could have. I never would have imagined growing up that I would have so much fun with
turns.zh: 能看得一清二楚。如今数据已经完美到信用利差（credit spreads）会同步变动。但在当时，这是一个全新的世界。你越努力、越深入钻研数据，你能获得的优势就越关键。我从小到大绝没想到，自己会在

turns.en: accounting. You know, accounting changes all the time. So it's like law. You've got to stay on top of things. And what was so interesting at the time was a lot of these companies, these subprime companies didn't incredibly well. The stocks just blew up. They absolutely didn't incredibly well
turns.zh: 会计上找到这么多乐趣。你知道，会计准则一直在变，所以它就像法律一样，你必须时刻紧跟。当时特别有意思的是，很多这类公司、这些次级贷款公司做得极其出色，股价直接暴涨。它们确实做得非常好，

turns.en: because what they did was if they were originating more and more and more, they would take what's called gain on sale accounting. So take a group of loans, take the upfront gains, and then amortize the expenses. So you're operating leverage was huge because you were accruing your
turns.zh: 因为他们的做法是：如果放贷规模越来越大，他们就会采用所谓的「销售利得会计法」（gain-on-sale accounting）。也就是把一组贷款的前端收益（upfront gains）先确认下来，再把费用摊销。所以你的经营杠杆（operating leverage）非常大，因为你在计提

turns.en: expenses, but then you did these huge upfront gains. And obviously that didn't trickle through the cash flows, but that ultimately changed. That was fast 115 versus fast 91. I'm such a dork. I can't believe I remember all of this was so long ago, but we knew this stuff. We took pride in
turns.zh: 费用的同时，又确认了这些巨额的前端收益。显然这并没有体现在现金流里，但这一点最终被改变了。那就是 FAS 115 对比 FAS 91。我真是个书呆子，真不敢相信这些陈年旧事我居然都还记得，但我们当时就是懂这些东西，还以此为荣。

turns.en: this stuff. I remember the top analyst at the time. I was at a conference and the MC who is now one of my closest professional friends asked the analyst about fast 91 and he didn't know what it was. And I was like, how can you I mean horrors? How can you not know what it was? But it was
turns.zh: 我记得当时那位顶级分析师。我在一个会议上，主持人（MC）——现在是我职场上最亲近的朋友之一——问那位分析师 FAS 91 是什么，他居然不知道。我心想：天哪，你怎么能不知道这是什么？但对

turns.en: a math geek's fantasy in terms of the data that was available and what was changing and how you could be precisely right. And then from a time in perspective, you had to be precisely right. You mentioned just of course your background is a history major. I tend to think a lot about
turns.zh: 数学极客来说，那简直是梦想成真——有那么多可得的数据、那么多变化，你能精确地判断对。而且从时机角度看，你必须精确地对。——你刚提到，当然你是历史专业出身。我常常思考

turns.en: historical risk episodes. Jim Chenos is going to come on the podcast in a couple of weeks and it's really to acknowledge. I wouldn't say the word is celebrate, but it's to acknowledge that we're coming up on 25 years of Enron and never before and hopefully never after as there been
turns.zh: 历史上的风险事件。Jim Chanos 几周后会上我们的播客，这其实是为了纪念——我不会用「庆祝」这个词，而是「纪念」——我们即将迎来 Enron 事件 25 周年。在此之前从未、希望此后也永不再有

turns.en: that much accounting to Canary. You can do a lot of things with accounting for sure. Very interestingly, you bring up Enron because it was my first year in oil and gas that I went to all of the road shows and all the analyst meetings. And at the time,
turns.zh: 那么多的会计造假（accounting chicanery）。——会计确实能做很多手脚。很有意思的是你提到了 Enron，因为我做油气的第一年就跑遍了所有路演（road show）和分析师会议。当时

turns.en: there was Enron, Annie, and Enron oil and gas. And both were big clients of Goldman Sachs. So I would go to Goldman Sachs and pay very close attention. So they were very much part of my world. And I remember them expanding into India and I knew the stories. That's 90 to 93 fast forward to
turns.zh: 有 Enron，还有 Enron Oil and Gas。它们都是 Goldman Sachs 的大客户。所以我会去 Goldman Sachs，特别留意。它们非常属于我的世界的一部分。我记得它们进军 India，那些故事我都知道。那是 1990 到 1993 年。快进到

turns.en: 2001. I was at Wacovia at the time. Here's the difference in disclosure. I knew that there were rumblings that something was going on with Enron. At the very same time, there was more attention paid to the fat that Argentina would default and what that would do to the banks. And I was covering
turns.zh: 2001 年。我当时在 Wachovia。这就是信息披露（disclosure）的差别。我知道当时有些风声，说 Enron 有问题。而与此同时，大家更多关注的是 Argentina 会不会违约、那会对银行造成什么影响。我当时覆盖的

turns.en: the banks at the time. I moved on from just coming special finance. And I remember writing a report that came out on December 1st. This is a report that I have in my library and my website, which was the Enron would be a much bigger risk to the banking system than Argentina. And I had
turns.zh: 正是银行。我已经从单纯做特殊金融转了出来。我记得我写了一份报告，在 12 月 1 日发布。这份报告现在还放在我的资料库和网站上，观点是：Enron 对银行体系的风险远比 Argentina 大。而且我掌握了

turns.en: the exposures of every single bank to Enron because that was the type of disclosure that existed back then. I would argue disclosure has gotten so much worse. You probably have more pages of disclosure, but the actual disclosure has gotten worse. So I was able to see that. And sure enough,
turns.zh: 每一家银行对 Enron 的风险敞口（exposure），因为那时候的信息披露就是这种类型。我要说，如今的披露其实变差了很多。披露的页数也许更多了，但真正有用的披露却变差了。所以我当时能看到这一点。果不其然，

turns.en: Enron declared bankruptcy, I think, over the holidays. But sure enough, that was one of the big daggers for the banks. And then you got into tech media telecom write downs of which, I think JP Morgan took close to $5 billion. That was huge at time of a write down associated with that. So
turns.zh: Enron 申请破产，我记得是在那个假期前后。果不其然，那是重创银行的其中一把匕首。接着又遇到了科技、媒体、电信（TMT）的减记，我记得 JPMorgan 减记了近 50 亿美元。在当时，那是一笔与此相关的巨额减记。所以

turns.en: it was another time for the banks back then. But careful what you lent you because everybody got swept up in how fabulous and fast paced Enron was, what they didn't know what was going on below the surface. But there were SPVs all over the place. Again, hiding in plain sight.
turns.zh: 对当时的银行来说又是一段艰难时期。但要小心你借钱给谁，因为所有人都被 Enron 有多么光鲜、节奏有多快给卷了进去，却不知道水面之下正在发生什么。到处都是特殊目的载体（SPV）。再一次，这些东西就藏在光天化日之下（hiding in plain sight）。

turns.en: Well, I took a spin of your website. And I love for you to just tell us what Meredith Whitney advisory group is doing for its clients. But I do want to read just something back from the website because I think it's going to underpin a lot of this conversation you wrote. There have been
turns.zh: 嗯，我逛了一下你的网站。我很想请你跟我们说说 Meredith Whitney Advisory Group 在为客户做些什么。不过我确实想从你网站里读一段话，因为我觉得它会支撑起我们这次对话的很多内容。你写道：「在我的职业生涯中，很少有

turns.en: fewer than a handful of times in my career when the financial markets have been this exciting with so much uncertainty in the markets. And in the health of the economy, my data has never served me better, being able to see around corners. Tell us your interactions with clients, what the

turns.zh: 真正起决定作用的是汽油价格和食品杂货，它只会让情况更糟。所以我常说，穷是一件极其昂贵的事，因为你为了拿到一点流动性（liquidity）所付的利率简直离谱。从一个层面看这非常悲哀。有人会站在另一边

turns.en: or it would be like, well, we're providing them liquidity that it wouldn't get otherwise. It's a death trap that's very hard to get out of. That said, if there's an emergency, at least there's some things there. It doesn't end well. Right now, losses across the border very low. If anyone's
turns.zh: 说：「可我们给他们提供了本来拿不到的流动性。」这是一个很难脱身的死亡陷阱。话虽如此，万一有紧急情况，至少还有些东西可用。但结局不会好。目前，各类贷款损失整体都非常低。如果有人想靠

turns.en: looking to banks to tell you how the economy is, this is something that sort of sticks in my crawl when everyone says, oh, the consumers resilient. Well, their consumers resilient because their consumers prime and super prime, that consumers unaffected by increased expenses. However,
turns.zh: 银行来判断经济状况如何，有件事让我很不爽：所有人都说「哦，消费者很有韧性」。可消费者有韧性，是因为他们是优质级和超优质级客户，这部分消费者不受开支上涨的影响。不过，

turns.en: there's one thing that I'm watching, which is again, the data that I love, you can get great data, recency data. And if you look at it the right way, it will tell you things. Obviously, one week does not make a trend. But the Fed puts out weekly data on revolving debt. And primarily,
turns.zh: 有一件事我一直在盯着——又是我喜爱的那些数据，你能拿到很好的、时效性很强的数据。如果你用对的方式去看，它会告诉你很多东西。显然，一周的数据成不了趋势。但 Fed 每周会发布循环债务（revolving debt）数据。而其中主要

turns.en: that's credit card debt. It's credit card loan balances. Since the beginning of the war, the Iran war, it's tracked in line with the growth in gas prices. Prior to September, gas prices peaked in May and growth in credit card balance peaked at that time. The movement was almost one for
turns.zh: 就是信用卡债务，是信用卡贷款余额。自这场战争——Iran 战争——开始以来，它与汽油价格的增长同步。在 9 月之前，汽油价格在 5 月见顶，信用卡余额的增长也在当时见顶。两者的走势几乎是

turns.en: one. That has started to break down recently. And what that tells me. So these are credit card balances, but that doesn't mean they're revolving balances. Primarily, they're not revolving balances because prime and super prime don't really revolve. So it's just where your balance is at a
turns.zh: 一比一的。这种关系最近开始脱钩了。这告诉我什么呢。这些是信用卡余额，但并不意味着它们是循环余额（revolving balances）。它们主要不是循环余额，因为优质级和超优质级客户基本不做循环借贷。所以这只是你在某个

turns.en: specific time in the month. When they're tracking one for one, that just means the consumers absorbing it, paying more, and they're overall spending it gets higher. When that diverges, it means that some of these households are making the very choices that the bottom of the K is making,
turns.zh: 时点上的余额。当两者一比一同步时，只意味着消费者在吸收这些成本、付得更多，整体开支也更高。当两者背离时，意味着其中一些家庭正在做出与 K 型底部人群完全相同的取舍，

turns.en: deciding, okay, I will get this and I won't get that because my gas prices are so much more. There's a great resource, and I know I'm biased as I went to Brown, but a great resource called the Iran war cost. They calculate on a daily basis what households,
turns.zh: 决定「好，这个我买，那个我就不买了，因为我的油费贵了这么多」。有一个很好的资源——我知道我有偏见，因为我是 Brown 毕业的——叫「Iran 战争成本」（Iran war cost）。他们每天计算家庭

turns.en: incredibly, are paying more on gas and diesel-related cost food and energy. And since end of February, it's close to $1,100 per household. The average household does not have $1,100 extra dollars. Famously, they barely have $400 for an emergency. So they have to make choices. That is going up the food chain. That is why I think the
turns.zh: 在汽油、柴油相关开支、食品和能源上多付了多少钱，数字令人震惊。自 2 月底以来，每个家庭接近 1100 美元。普通家庭根本拿不出 1100 美元的闲钱。众所周知，他们连应对紧急情况的 400 美元都勉强。所以他们必须做取舍。这种影响正在沿着链条向上传导。这就是为什么我认为

turns.en: prediction markets got Israel wrong, too. They're showing Democrats win by a big margin. We'll see next week, but the fundamentals to me, not looking at polls, tell me that it's going to be a blood bath. Well, we talked about the pre-GFC period. And that's a period where the economy is doing well,
turns.zh: 预测市场在 Israel 上也判断错了。它们现在显示 Democrats 会以很大优势获胜。下周就见分晓，但对我来说，不看民调、只看基本面，告诉我那将会是一场血洗。——好，我们谈了全球金融危机（GFC）之前的那段时期。那是一段经济表现不错的时期，

turns.en: but in some ways, it's a house of cards built on mortgage derivatives and just continuing to extend credit to a dice year and dice year set of folks in terms of paying it back. And I see no mortgage fraud right now or leverage in the banking system, but I do see an economy that has
turns.zh: 但从某些方面看，它是一座建立在抵押贷款衍生品（mortgage derivatives）之上的纸牌屋，还在不断向还款能力越来越差（dicier and dicier）的人群发放信贷。我现在看不到抵押贷款欺诈、也看不到银行体系里的杠杆，但我确实看到一个已经

turns.en: gotten very AI CapEx-centric so that if you were just to look at top line nominal GDP growth, you'd say, oh, this isn't too bad. You're painting a picture on an ether surface that's really bad. And so what I'd love to do is just finish by soliciting some of your thoughts on
turns.zh: 变得非常以 AI 资本开支（AI CapEx）为中心的经济，以至于如果你只看名义 GDP 的顶线增长，你会说「哦，还不错」。但你描绘的是一幅水面之下其实很糟糕的图景。所以最后我想请你谈谈对

turns.en: this AI CapEx trade. I think in a recent appearance on Bloomberg, I saw you talk about the circularity and said something to the notion of it's all one trade. And so in terms of looking around corners, and you look at this path-breaking technology, probably really matters for years to
turns.zh: 这笔 AI 资本开支交易的看法。我记得你最近上 Bloomberg 时谈到了其中的循环性（circularity），大意是「这全都是同一笔交易」。那么从「看清拐角后面」的角度，你看着这项开创性的技术——它很可能在未来很多年都真正

turns.en: come. What do you see there when you look at just the big picture of the AI build out? It's telling when Larry Fink is going around and telling people if we slow down AI, we'll go into a recession. That may be absolutely true, but the concentration, just even looking at the market,
turns.zh: 重要。当你只看 AI 建设（AI build-out）的大局时，你看到了什么？——当 Larry Fink 四处对人们说「如果我们放慢 AI，就会陷入衰退」时，这很说明问题。那也许完全属实，但光是看市场的集中度（concentration），

turns.en: you look at the indices and it looks like, oh great, this market, this has been a fairly decent year. But what's underneath the surface is stocks are down double digits. I mean, this has been a horrible year for active managers if they don't own the stocks. It's not even the MAG-7.
turns.zh: 你看那些指数，会觉得「哦，太好了，这个市场今年是相当不错的一年」。但水面之下，很多股票跌了两位数。我是说，对于主动管理者（active managers）来说，今年是糟糕的一年，只要他们没持有那几只股票。而且集中度甚至不只是「七巨头」（Mag 7）。

turns.en: The concentration is so intense. And I think that that's true in the capital markets as well. Again, it's very hard to note timing. And this is inspiring me to actually do a little rabbit holeing on the leverage of Cory. We've was hiding in plain sight for a year. It'll be
turns.zh: 这种集中度太剧烈了。我觉得在资本市场上也是如此。再说一次，时机很难判断。而这正激励我要真的去深挖一下核心（core）的杠杆问题。这个隐患已经在光天化日之下藏了一年。届时

turns.en: interesting to see how investors feel about the stocks that really grew based on stock buybacks. When they don't buy any stockback, they don't have excess cash flow. What happens to those names and they're just issuing more and more equity? It's a reversal of what propelled the MAG-7
turns.zh: 看看投资者会如何看待那些真正靠股票回购（stock buybacks）成长起来的股票，会很有意思。当它们不再回购、又没有多余现金流时会怎样？那些标的会怎么样，而它们还在不断增发股票？这正是三年前推动「七巨头」（Mag 7）

turns.en: three years ago. It's so interesting. It's sort of like this push and pull between debt financing and equity financing and which one is more expensive as you just demand more and more capital. It's just so different than, you know, it seemed like once the system repaired itself and it
turns.zh: 上涨的动力的反转。——太有意思了。这有点像债务融资（debt financing）和股权融资（equity financing）之间的拉锯，以及在你不断索取越来越多资本时，哪一种更贵。这与过去太不同了，你知道，一旦这个系统自我修复——而且

turns.en: took years, as you said, there was this sense of just excess capital and rates were not zero, but damn, they're close to zero. What are the risks that we ought to be thinking about and where might they be underappreciated and then where might there just be opportunity on the long side,
turns.zh: 像你说的花了好几年——就有一种资本过剩的感觉，利率虽不是零，但天哪，已经很接近零了。那么我们应该思考哪些风险？哪些风险可能被低估了？而在多头（long side）上又可能存在哪些机会，

turns.en: you know, outside of Dave and Shine, like what are some of the things that you think the market's just kind of missing from a investment perspective? This isn't my area of expertise, but these are just like the basics, which is I don't understand why the forward curve on oil assumes the oil will
turns.zh: 你知道，除了 Dave 和 Chime 之外，从投资角度看，你认为市场忽略了一些什么东西？——这不是我的专长领域，但这些只是最基本的东西：我不明白为什么石油的远期曲线（forward curve）假定明年油价会

turns.en: be lower next year than this year. That makes no sense to me because the presumption that the straight of hormones will open up and everything will be fine. The over-promising of a peace deal has been on rinse and repeat. It has disappointed every single time. The fact that oil is going down
turns.zh: 比今年低。这在我看来毫无道理，因为它的预设是霍尔木兹海峡（Strait of Hormuz）会重新开放、一切都会没事。对和平协议的过度承诺一直在反复上演，每一次都让人失望。油价明年会下跌这件事，

turns.en: next year makes no sense to me whatsoever. These names have worked, but I don't think they've worked to the extent that they should work. I think Chevron reports this week or next week, I own a bunch of it. That's been a no-brainer for me. Looking off of the assumption, again,
turns.zh: 在我看来根本说不通。这些标的一直有效，但我不认为它们的表现达到了应有的程度。我想 Chevron 这周或下周发财报，我持有不少，这对我来说是不用动脑的选择。同样是基于那个假设——再说一次，

turns.en: does not make any sense to me that oil will be down, imitories and reserves. All right, at all times low, you have to re-boat that. They'll be hoarding. That makes no sense. What that means then is the case shape gets wider and wider because this pressure continues. And so the names
turns.zh: 油价会下跌在我看来毫无道理——库存和储备一直都很低，你必须重新补充（rebuild）。他们会囤积。这说不通。那么这意味着，K 型分化会越来越宽，因为这种压力持续存在。所以我们讨论的

turns.en: that we discuss, the chime, the Dave, the block, all of that, sadly, those continue to do well. I see inflation being a very tough thing to tamp down and this is nothing that the fed can control. They can't control the cost of oil or diesel. That to me is the biggest head scratcher. You know
turns.zh: 那些标的——Chime、Dave、Block——很遗憾，它们会继续表现不错。我认为通胀（inflation）是非常难压下去的，而这根本不是 Fed 能控制的。他们控制不了石油或柴油的成本。对我来说这是最让人费解的地方。你知道，

turns.en: if something's going to happen with NeoClouds, AI's not priced for risk at all, we'll see the energy complex is the most obvious to me now. Some part of our conversation is I would say maybe the song remains the same that it's never different this time so you can always look back and
turns.zh: 如果 NeoClouds 要出什么事的话——AI 根本没有为风险定价——我们会看到的。能源板块（energy complex）在我看来是最明显的。——我们这次对话有一部分，我会说，也许是「老调重弹」：从来就没有「这次不一样」，所以你总能回头看，

turns.en: have some appreciation for how these things tend to reboot themselves, maybe in different format. But at the same time, I think you said it earlier in the conversation, things evolve. You have to evolve your process as well. If you were to just big picture think about your process today versus
turns.zh: 对这些事情往往会以不同形式重演有所体会。但与此同时，我想你在对话前面说过，事情会演变，你的方法论也必须随之演变。如果你从大局来看你今天的方法论，对比

turns.en: I don't know a decade ago, what's new? There's new data. There's some new technology to analyze the data. How are you doing your craft today a little bit differently than maybe a decade ago? Let's go back when I first started. I would go to the library to research and now everything's
turns.zh: 比如说十年前，有什么新东西？有新数据，有分析数据的新技术。你今天做这行的方式，跟十年前比有什么不同？——回到我刚入行的时候，我会去图书馆做研究，而现在一切都

turns.en: at your fingertips. AI gets a lot of things wrong in your arguing with it because the validation is so poor. From a search engine perspective, I have my own sources but they perhaps will find sources different than I would necessarily so the scope of research and data sources is so much
turns.zh: 触手可及。AI 会把很多事情搞错，你还得跟它争，因为它的验证能力太差了。从搜索引擎的角度看，我有自己的信息源，但 AI 也许能找到一些跟我不一定相同的来源，所以研究和数据源的范围大了

turns.en: bigger but you have to check every last thing because you can't assume and this is the risk for younger people. You can't assume that what you're getting from AI is accurate because I would say at least 75% of the time it's not and it's early days but it's just not. Over the years,
turns.zh: 很多，但你必须逐条核实，因为你不能想当然——这对年轻人来说是个风险。你不能假定从 AI 得到的东西是准确的，因为我会说至少 75% 的情况下它并不准确，而且现在还只是早期，但它就是不准。这些年下来，

turns.en: data has just gotten better. The data out of the government's gotten worse and less reliable and that's too bad. So you just adjust. Yeah, talking my own book here is someone who's been in this business for a long time. I do think the overlay of human judgment at the end of it. I don't see
turns.zh: 数据只是变得更好了。政府出的数据却变差了、更不可靠了，这很遗憾。所以你只能去适应。是啊，我这么说有点王婆卖瓜，毕竟我在这行待了很久。我确实认为，最终还是要叠加人的判断（human judgment），我不觉得

turns.en: that going away. So it's all about perspective and you've brought us a lot of that today. Meredith, I'm really glad we got a chance to do this. I'm going to thank you again for introducing us. Thanks for being a guest. Oh, we were great interviewer. So thank you so much. This is fun.
turns.zh: 这一点会消失。——所以一切都关乎视角，而你今天给我们带来了很多这样的视角。Meredith，我真的很高兴我们有机会做这次对谈。我要再次感谢把我们介绍认识。谢谢你来当嘉宾。——哦，你是个很棒的采访者，非常感谢你，这很有意思。

turns.en: your input is valuable and provides direction. I'm where we should focus. Please email us at feedback at alphaexchangepodcast.com. Thanks again and catch you next time.
